title: 任务父子关系允许跨项目，并可被项目内硬删除级联删除跨项目子任务
head: 138cf2da1b63195cef7e884f69bdf8ded6ed3c21
entrypoint: POST /api/sync/push tasks parentId followed by PUT /api/projects/:projectAId with a task replacement array
preconditions: A project-B sync writer can submit a task with projectId=B and parentId referencing a project-A task; historical B19 probe demonstrated the edge can be established.
A project-A editor with project write capability submits task replacement; historical B02 probe demonstrated the route physically deletes project-A task rows without a task.delete check.
The deployed database applies the current migration-defined task parent FK with ON DELETE CASCADE; production schema drift was not inspected.

source.symbol: task guard validates phase, not parent project
task replacement runs project-scoped physical deleteMany
database FK parent_id references tasks.id ON DELETE CASCADE

callPath: Project B sync writer creates a Project-B task with parentId pointing to Project A (historically accepted; source still permits it).
Project A edit route checks project write capability and processes tasksInput.
The route executes tx.task.deleteMany({where:{projectId:A}}), a physical delete of omitted A tasks.
The migration-defined parent_id FK cascades a physical delete to any child row referencing that parent, without a projectId predicate.

evidence.limitation: Historical isolated probe demonstrated the cross-project parent edge can be established; this cross-project parent deletion sequence was not part of that probe.
Historical isolated probe demonstrated project task replacement physically removes task rows without task.delete; cross-project child cascade was not measured.
Current route, Prisma relation, and migration FK define the connected path. No single end-to-end DB reproduction or production DB schema inspection was run.

counterevidenceChecked: The operation still requires the actor to edit Project A; it does not grant read access to Project B.
Project capability/system permission checks remain before replacement, but the nested deletion does not check tasks.delete.
The FK cascade is on physical parent deletion; soft deletion alone does not fire this FK.
Current production database constraint drift is unknown.
observedImpact: The historical probes establish both preconditions separately, and current source/schema establish that, when both conditions hold and the target DB follows the checked migration, deleting the parent row physically deletes its cross-project child through FK cascade. The combined outcome was not dynamically observed.
potentialImpact: A Project-A editor may unintentionally or deliberately remove a task row owned by Project B by replacing Project-A tasks after a cross-project edge was inserted. Trigger requires the cross-project edge and physical deletion; actual deployed schema and combined runtime are not verified.
recommendation: Validate parentId project ownership and acyclicity at every write entry; prevent project task replacement from physically deleting protected child rows; scope recursive/cascade behavior by project and move deletion to authorized tombstone commands. Before changes, read-only inventory cross-project edges and review any cascade-dependent behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: Cross-project parent creation is rejected in sync and any future HTTP path.
A Project-A editor cannot cause a Project-B task to be physically removed through a Project-A replacement payload.
Approved deletion semantics preserve project isolation, tombstone propagation and dependent records.
Historical anomaly inventory is reviewed before adding stricter FK constraints.
pendingQuestions: Confirm deployed database constraint matches the initial migration.
Count cross-project edges on an authorized read-only data source; decide repair before migration.
supplementalChange: Impact extension based on combined historical B02/B19 evidence and current source/FK contract; ID and severity unchanged.
